newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia to sell stake in oil distribution firm.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia to sell stake in oil distribution firm.

text.p: Tunisia plans to launch a public offer to sell up to 30 percent in the country's major petrol distribution company, Societe Nationale de Distribution des Petroles (SNDP), known under the commercial name of AGIL.
The company will raise its capital before selling shares, chairman Charfeddine Guellouz said on Wednesday at a meeting with the company's 180 filling-station managers.
They quoted Guellouz as saying the company had completed work on its plan to raise capital but the exact share to be sold had yet to be decided.
Fully owned by the Tunisian state, SNDP has a 2.95 million dinars ($2.73 million) capital. Its turnover in 1996 was 386 million dinars, up from 358 million dinars in 1995.
AGIL is the leader in petrol distribution with about 50 percent of the market, ahead of privately-owned Tunisian subsidiaries of Esso, Total, Shell, Mobil and Elf, industry sources said.
The public offer was expected in the next few months and the company would then be listed on the Tunis Stock Exchange, bourse sources said.
SNDP was established in 1975 after the Tunisian state purchased the 50 percent stake of Italian energy group ENI in Agip Tunisia S.A. which was distributing petrol under the AGIP brand name.
It has three petrol depots -- in the port of La Goulette, in the southern city of Sfax and at Tunis-Carthage airport -- as well 180 filling stations nationwide.

It also distributes domestic and industrial liquefied petroleum gas and produces and sells lubricants in partnership with Italy's Agip Spa lubricants division. ($=1.08 dinars) -- Tunis newsroom 2161-787538
